Is there an emergency dentist on Koh Samui? | The private hospitals in Chaweng and Bophut run dental departments and 24-hour emergency rooms, and private dental clinics on the main roads see walk-in patients during the day. At night or on a Sunday, go to a hospital emergency department for pain relief and a dental appointment.
How much is a dental check-up on Koh Samui? | Expect roughly 300–800 THB for a check-up and consultation and 800–2,000 THB for a scale and polish at a private clinic, with hospital dental departments at the upper end. Ask for the price before you sit in the chair.
How do I check a Thai dentist is licensed? | Ask for the dentist's full name and look it up in the public "Check Dentists" search on the Dental Council of Thailand's website. Every dentist practising in Thailand must be registered with the Council.
Can I get implants done during a 30-day stay? | Rarely in full. The implant usually needs 3–6 months to heal before the crown is fitted, so most people need two trips or a long-stay visa. Fillings, cleaning and most crowns fit easily into 30 days.
Can I fly or dive after a tooth extraction? | Ask your dentist for a specific date. Many advise waiting at least 24 hours before flying after an extraction, and longer after surgery, and divers are generally advised not to dive for several days to a week afterwards.
Does travel insurance cover dental treatment? | Usually only emergency treatment for sudden pain, up to a low limit. Planned work such as crowns, veneers or implants is almost never covered, so call your insurer before treatment and keep itemised receipts.
What should I do if my face swells from a tooth infection? | Go to a hospital emergency department the same day, or call 1669 if you have a fever, difficulty swallowing or breathing. A spreading dental infection needs antibiotics and urgent care, not just a dentist's appointment.
How long does a crown take on Koh Samui? | Usually two visits about a week apart: one to prepare the tooth and take impressions or a scan, and one to fit the finished crown. Some clinics make crowns in-house faster; allow extra time for adjustments before you fly.
